program: <short name, lower case: it names the agents and the watchdog, e.g. helpdesk>
repo: <owner/name of the target repository; a stream may name its own>

streams.name: <stream, e.g. portal>
streams.writable: <the paths this stream may write, e.g. `portal/**`, `shared/ui/**`>
streams.ports: <how an item's port is worked out, for people: `HD-nn` serves on `84nn`. With `port_base` the scripts work it out: base plus the item's number. Leave `port_base` out for a stream that serves nothing.>

run.work: <what this run completes, as the operator would say it: Help desk portal>
run.file: <the stream's first backlog file, beside this spec>

settings.claude_config_dir: <optional: the seat the program starts on, one of the template's `claude_seats` (a ~/.claude-<name> directory with its own Claude sign-in); leave the key out to start on the first of them. Never the host's default ~/.claude: that sign-in is the operator's own>
settings.outside_prs: <optional: `adopt` or `off` (merge no pull request a steward labels rollout-ready); leave the key out for the template's `off` on a new program, or for what a program staged again already has>
outside_pr_vetters: <the GitHub login a steward labels and comments with; only these count, and none named (the key left out) means nothing is adopted. Staging takes them from this spec alone, so removing one here revokes it>
settings.outside_pr_shared_login: <optional: `accept` only if the stewards' login is also the one the loop's token acts as, knowing a worker could then mark its own pull request ready (every such merge then says so, and the ledger shows it); left out, `refuse`: nothing merges in that case. Staging takes it from this spec alone>

prompt.FILES_AND_GATES: <every backlog file in order, each with its run id and run directory, and the gates between them, each written for the manager to get done (references/authoring.md, Gates are the manager's). {{ROOT}} and {{TASK_DIR}} are filled in.>
prompt.PRODUCTION_BOUNDARY: <what is production and must not be touched, and what is the program's to change; never a credential or a gate put out of the manager's reach>
prompt.CAPACITY: <how many streams and workers at once, and the measurement that decides: start nothing under 20 % free memory>
prompt.ACCOUNT_SHARING: <who else uses the workers' Claude account while this runs>
prompt.ROUTING_NOTES: <optional: what this program's manager should know when it routes, beyond the kit's defaults; leave the key out for none>

facts: <a sentence every worker in this repository is told: a tool version CI uses, a condition of the test host that is known and is not a finding>
<owner/name>.setup: <one command line that makes a fresh checkout ready (dependencies installed), writing only paths git ignores>
setup_inputs: <each file that command's result depends on: lockfiles, requirement files>
ci_covers: <`check name`: what that required check runs>
not_in_ci: <a suite no required check runs, as the command that runs it>
seen: <glob of paths that hold what a person sees: templates, styles, components>
protected: <glob of paths no item may change: generated or pinned files>
exemptable: <optional: glob of protected paths the manager may exempt for one named item (`hl-items exempt`); leave the key out for none>
<owner/name>.reference: <optional: one directory of the repository holding the pages a look is compared with, such as `brand`; served beside a looked-at build. Leave the key out for none>
deploys: <the workflow file that deploys the repository on a push to the base, such as `apply-main.yml`: an outside pull request's deploy check reads its runs. `[]` where a merge deploys nothing; left out, no outside pull request merges in this repository>
